Subject: Partial streaming completions timing out -> 5xx + client retry surge

Jonas / Redwood ops,

We started seeing a pattern around 13:40 UTC where a subset of interactive streaming completions for our clinical note generator time out at ~15s. The client closes the connection and immediately retries, which in turn pushes a lot of traffic back at your endpoint and we begin to see 429 responses and occasional 5xx bursts.

Quick reproduction notes:
- Region: us-central (api.redwood.com)
- Model: redwood-chat-l8 (pinned)
- Typical traffic: 120 concurrent sessions per shard during window
- Symptoms: intermittent partial payloads (stream ended mid-token) followed by client retries within 200-700ms of disconnect

I've attached a short session dump and a pcap of the connection window. We can reproduce consistently with our load generator and are currently throttling at our side to stop the amplification.

Can you confirm whether you saw any infra events (NLB scale, kernel restarts, or backend pod OOMs) in that time window? Also, is there any recent change to idle timeouts / TCP keepalive defaults on the public gateway?

-Maya
Ops Lead, Lanterna Health

Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 15:03:44 -0000
Subject: Re: Partial streaming completions timing out -> 5xx + client retry surge

Investigated infra metrics for the 13:30-14:00 UTC window:
- No pod OOMs or restarts in the model pool.
- NLB showed elevated connection churn; idle connection count dropped for ~2m before steadying.
- Backend error rate (5xx) spiked from 0.1% -> 2.7% for a narrow shard set; token-serving latency increased ~60ms p90.

Prelim hypothesis: a subset of clients are closing streams prematurely (client-side hard timeouts), which causes rapid retries. Those retries concentrate on a small set of warm workers that had less KV cache priming, producing higher CPU and triggering transient 5xx responses. This then feeds back into more retries.

Short-term mitigations proposed (we can implement within 30m):
- Temporary soft-rate-limit on duplicate concurrent starts from same client IP / API key for 3m windows.
- Increase gateway idle timeout from 30s -> 45s to tolerate longer client-side reconnections.
- Add a small 100ms jittered backoff on our public client SDK (patch) and push a hotfix to CDN (we can ship today).

Attachments: tcp-trace-20280320.pcap

I'll start a small canary of the rate-limit and idle timeout change; will report back once metrics show improvement.

- Aditya
SRE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Leadership,

Summary: Lanterna (strategic mid-market customer, onboarding to Dedicated next quarter) is experiencing a retry amplification pattern that results in short-lived 5xx bursts and a persistent stream partial-completion failure mode for certain clients. The customer has reproducible sessions and has already begun local throttling to avoid their own outage. Current status:
- Incident window: 2028-03-20T13:35 -> ongoing (mitigations in flight)
- Observed impact: elevated 5xx spikes (up to 2.7% for impacted shards), increased token latency p90, and a rise in 429s due to retry storms
- Business risk: customer-facing production degradation; onboarding timeline at risk; CS escalated to leadership

Actions taken so far:
1) Applied per-key soft ratelimit canary (rolling) — initial telemetry shows 35% reduction in concurrent restarts from repeated client starts.
2) Increased gateway idle timeout to 45s in the canary region.
3) Preparing a hotfix to SDK to recommend exponential backoff and increase default client keepalive.

Requested decisions:
- Approve broad rollback of any recent gateway tuning that reduced idle timeouts (if present) — Aditya, please confirm config delta.
- Approve a short-term customer credit / SLA buffer if onboarding deadlines slip (CS/Rev ops to propose amount).
- Approve a small emergency engineering rotation to prioritize a permanent fix for keepalive-handling and kv-cache warmup behaviour.

Want to align on 11:00 UTC quick sync today to confirm next steps and who will brief Sales/RevOps.

—Jonas
